What did we learn last week?

What is an entrepreneur?

Someone who turns an idea into a business and takes the risk to make it real.

What is a stock?

A tiny piece of a company. Own a share, own a slice.

Why do people invest in companies?

If the company grows, their piece can become worth more.

Stock Market Challenge

How’s the market doing?

The stock market changes every day. Investing rewards research, discipline, and long-term thinking, but returns are never guaranteed.

Stock Market Challenge

What is market cap?

Market cap is what all of a company’s shares are worth together.

Market Cap =Share Price × Shares

Whole pizza = market cap

One slice = one share

Understanding the stock market

Why do people look at market cap?

How big is it?

It shows the size of the whole company, not just one share.

Who’s bigger?

It lets us compare companies fairly, even when share prices are very different.

Steady or risky?

Big companies tend to be steadier. Small ones can grow faster, but they’re riskier.

Understanding the stock market

Same size pizza, different slices

Netflix
Share price$69
Shares4.2 billion
Market cap≈ $291 billion
Home Depot
Share price$285
Shares1.0 billion
Market cap≈ $284 billion

Home Depot’s shares cost 4× more, but both companies are worth about the same. Netflix just cut its pizza into more slices.

Understanding the stock market

Same slices, different size burger

Microsoft
Share price$527
Shares7.4 billion
Market cap≈ $3.9 trillion
Walmart
Share price$106
Shares8.0 billion
Market cap≈ $845 billion

Almost the same number of shares, but Microsoft is worth about 4½× more. Each Microsoft slice is a bigger bite.

Understanding the stock market

Bull market vs. bear market

Bull market

Prices keep rising for a long stretch. Investors feel confident.

A bull attacks by swinging its horns up.

Bear market

Prices fall 20% or more from their high. Investors get nervous.

A bear attacks by swiping its paws down.

Would you rather invest in a bull market or a bear market? Why?

Welcome Mr. Mettler!

Guest speaker

What is entrepreneurship?

Turning ideas into something real
See a problem

Notice something that could be better.

Imagine a solution

Come up with an idea to solve it.

Take action

Turn your idea into a product, service, or business.

Entrepreneurs don’t just have ideas. They do something with them!
Entrepreneurship

They started young

Cory Nieves
Mr. Cory’s Cookies

Started selling cookies at age 6 in Englewood, New Jersey.

Rachel Zietz
Gladiator Lacrosse

Started a lacrosse gear company at 13 because the gear she used kept breaking.

MrBeast
Creator & builder

Started making YouTube videos at 13. Now he also sells Feastables chocolate.

Entrepreneurship

Traits of entrepreneurs

CuriosityAsks “why?” and “what if?”
GritKeeps going when things get hard.
TeamworkBuilds a team where everyone brings something different.
PassionReally cares about the problem they’re solving.
FocusFinishes what they start.
Entrepreneurship

Your entrepreneur toolkit

1
Start small

Try a simple version first.

2
Learn fast

Mistakes teach you what to fix.

3
Ask for help

Parents, teachers, and mentors want to help.

4
Know your why

Who are you helping, and why does it matter?

5
Write it down

Ideas become plans when you write them down.

Entrepreneurship

What’s your idea?

What’s a problem at school, at home, or in our community that someone could solve with a product or service?

“You get to build the future, one idea at a time.”
